title: Left without beeing seen (LWBS)/Left before treatment is complete (LBTC)- Characterization of a specific patient group in the emergency room
summary: Against the backdrop of ever-growing challenges in emergency care for patients in central emergency departments and in view of the upcoming reform of emergency care in Germany, efficient patient management, relief for emergency departments, and economically efficient emergency care are essential. One relevant component of this is the consideration of a special group of patients known internationally as Left Without Being Seen (LWBS). The LWBS patient collective comprises patients who leave the emergency department after undergoing an initial medical assessment (Medical Screening Examination, MSE) but before diagnostic measures have been taken and before emergency care has been completed, without having been seen by medical staff and thus without undergoing a structured treatment process. This must be distinguished from the patient subgroup “Left Before Treatment is Complete” (LBTC), who leave the emergency room after undergoing an initial medical assessment and initial diagnostic measures, but before contacting a physician, i.e., before emergency care is completed. The LWBS/LBTC patient collective poses a growing challenge for the healthcare system, particularly with regard to the quality of care and patient safety.

interventions.name: Retrospective single-arm study characterizing the LWBS patient collective over a period of 3 years.
